title: Week in Orbit
summary: A week marked by significant developments in military satellite contracts and corporate maneuvering, as SpaceX and Blue Origin both make strides in their respective projects. Meanwhile, the Space Force and NASA are reshaping their strategic priorities amidst a backdrop of evolving global threats.

themes.title: Military Satellite Network Expansion
themes.body: The Space Force's hefty $437 million contract with Viasat and SES signals a robust push towards enhancing military satellite capabilities. This investment reflects an increasing recognition of the need for resilient space infrastructure amid growing geopolitical tensions.

themes.title: Blue Origin's Launch Recovery
themes.body: After a thorough investigation into the New Glenn launch failure, Blue Origin is poised to regain its footing in the competitive launch market. The resolution of this setback could be pivotal for its future contracts and credibility.

themes.title: SpaceX's Starship V3 Launch
themes.body: SpaceX's launch of the first Starship V3 marks another milestone in its ambitious plans for space exploration and commercial ventures. This development not only showcases their technological prowess but also sets the stage for future endeavors in the burgeoning space economy.

themes.title: AUKUS and Strategic Space Infrastructure
themes.body: The focus on building Australia’s dual-use space infrastructure underscores the strategic importance of collaboration within the AUKUS alliance. This initiative is a clear indication of how nations are leveraging space capabilities to bolster defense and resilience.
